title: A typed inventory
description:
Write an inventory with full type hints, generic containers and a `TypedDict` for its saved form, and check it with a type checker.

```
inventory: 3 items, total value 151.50
saved as JSON, loaded back: equal
mypy: Success: no issues found
```
hints: `class Repository[T]:` with a `dict[int, T]` inside; give it a function that tells it how to read an id from a `T` (lesson 8.03).
The checker cannot see inside JSON, so `from_dict` must check each field itself before building an `Item`.
requirements: A generic `Repository[T]` with `add`, `get(id) -> T | None` and `all() -> list[T]`.
`Item` as a dataclass and `ItemDict` as a `TypedDict` for saving; `to_dict` and `from_dict` convert between them, checking types when loading.
Every function has parameter and return hints; run `mypy` or `pyright` on your own machine.
stretch: Add a `Protocol` called `HasId` and use it as the bound: `class Repository[T: HasId]`.
